messages:
jamie: heads up — after yesterday's outbound firewall tightening in eu-west we started seeing conntrack exhaustion on NATs which is backpressuring GPU node booting. noticed a spike in `nf_conntrack_count` on the egress fleet.
sofia: yikes. saw any KMS/decrypt errors?
jamie: yes, some nodes failed during bootstrap with `keystore: decrypt timed out` and stack shows repeated `EPIPE` to privatelink endpoints. sample log: `2024-06-01T07:12:43Z keystore: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing`
leo: that matches conntrack overflow — existing conntrack max is 65536 on the NATs. during warmup we create ~80k short-lived flows due to probes + image pulls + KMS.
priya: what's the immediate mitigation? rollback the fw rule?
jamie: want to avoid full rollback. propose: 1) bump conntrack hashsize/max (sysctl) on NATs, 2) enable conntrack tcp-timeout tweaks for TIME_WAIT, 3) add short-term KMS egress connection pooling from nodes (reuse), 4) add audit sampling to keystore logs to reduce log write IOPS cost.
sofia: agree. can we do quick patch for sysctl first? command: ```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=30```
leo: LGTM but need change on the autoscaling NAT ASGs too. I'll prepare an AMI bake with the sysctl in /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf and push via FleetRoll.
jamie: also adding iptables conntrack helper for short flows: ```-A POSTROUTING -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j CONNMARK --set-mark 0x1``` — helps classify.
priya: for KMS, can we burst-limit clients instead of NAT? maybe client-side backoff + connection pooling implemented in our keystore agent.
jamie: yes, I've got a keystore agent patch ready: reuse TLS sessions and a small in-process connection pool. will open PR today.
sofia: about audit logs — current setting streams every keystore request to longterm S3; with sampling we reduce write rate. sec-bot, any compliance concerns?
sec-bot: sampling allowable for operational logs but must maintain 100% for auth/crypto key events. Suggest: sample non-crypto metadata at 10% and keep full logs for `decrypt`/`encrypt` events. Record sampling config in the audit policy repo.
leo: noted. I'll update the audit policy: `audit.keystore.sample_rate: 0.1` for metadata.
infra-bot: rolling conntrack sysctl to eu-west NATs: started 3/6 instances (1m delay between). Monitoring conntrack_count and node boot success.
jamie: baseline metrics to watch: `nf_conntrack_count`, `keystore_decrypt_errors`, `gpu_node_boot_time_ms`, `nat_conntrack_drops`. Let's put an alert: `NF_CONNTRACK_USED > 75% for 5m` -> pager.
priya: cost question — bumping conntrack isn't costly, but enabling more NAT capacity might increase NAT gateway charges if we move to managed NATs. prefer tuning first.
sofia: agree. if we need more capacity long-term, consider VPC endpoints for KMS/privatelink to reduce NAT egress.
leo: quick rollout plan: (a) sysctl + conntrack conf via AMI and FleetRoll (b) keystore agent pooling PR + canary (c) audit sampling policy update (d) revisit fw rule if residual drop.
jamie: can someone own (b) and (c)? priya take the keystore agent PR, leo take audit policy edit?
priya: taking (b). will open PR and add feature flag `keystore.pooling=true` for canary clusters.
leo: taking (c). will add policy, ping sec for signoff.
jamie: thanks. infra-bot — keep posting roll progress and metrics. once we confirm node bootstrap rates normalized we'll close the thread. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: conntrack_count eu-west NATs back to ~40k after first 3 instances updated. gpu node boot success rate improved from 86% -> 96% in canary ASG. ongoing.
sec-bot: audit policy PR linked: https://git.internal/r/audit/pulls/42 — sample config attached.
sofia: great. let's check again in 2 hours and decide if further egress changes are needed.
